results.why: Each relic has exactly ONE emotion, but the app records no emotion for it, so authoring the record as printed stars ten skills for a character who gets one. Ruling C says star everything that could be it, but ruling C covered bonuses that genuinely could hit any of several stats at the moment of use; here nine of the ten are permanently false for this character, which is closer to ruling A's 'they should only see the options they can have'. Choosing between them is a call about how much the app should model versus display, and it is the same unresolved shape as Weapon Innovation, which is still parked on your go-ahead. Note one part IS decidable and needs no ruling: the Dedication row reads 'Checks to Recall Knowledge', which is any skill, so skill 'all' is correct.

results.recommend: Option 2, the picker. The choose-one-of-N picker and the item choice surface both already ship, so the authoring side is routine; what is genuinely new is that the situational registry keys entries by owned record id only and has no way to gate a star on a pick, so this is engine work, not data. If you don't want that work now, option 3 beats option 1 — nine wrong stars are worse than none, and the advanced item editor already covers the player who wants it.

results.answer: Registry, not Modes — and yes, it renders penalties. Item modes can only be switched on by useConsumable, which drops the quantity and deletes the item at the last one; that is wrong for a permanent worn item, so activated-buff items with a duration belong in the registry with the duration written into `when` (exactly how the Six-Fingers Elixir and Stalwart's Banner entries already read). Register: strikeAttack +1 status, when 'against the target for 1 minute after a successful Bragging Rights Strike'; strikeAttack -1 status 'against the target for 1 round on a failure'; strikeAttack -2 status 'on a critical failure'. 'You and your allies' includes you, so ruling F does not suppress it.
